467	    starts, which stretch of days each fixed value holds over, which suppositions
468	    something undermined and on which day, and what the reader should be warned
469	    about. All of it is the same in every one of the sixteen thousand draws, which
470	    is exactly why it is computed once.
471	
472	    Args:
473	        graph: The map a fold left behind.
474	        assignments: Every value that fold fixed, in order.
475	        as_of: Day zero.
476	
477	    Returns:
478	        Everything the draw below needs and nothing that depends on a seed.
479	    """
480	    claims = {one.id: one for one in graph.propositions}
481	    ordinary = _ordinary_arrows(graph, claims)
482	    order = _causes_before_effects(claims, ordinary)
483	    arrows_into: dict[PropositionId, tuple[Link, ...]] = {
484	        claim_id: tuple(one for one in ordinary if one.target == claim_id) for claim_id in claims
485	    }
486	
487	    fixed_on: dict[PropositionId, list[Assignment]] = {claim_id: [] for claim_id in claims}
488	    for one in assignments:
489	        if one.target in fixed_on:
490	            fixed_on[one.target].append(one)
491	    settled = _settled_days(order, arrows_into, fixed_on, as_of)
492	
493	    days = _window_length(graph, as_of)
494	    points = _days_to_work_out(claims, as_of, days)
495	    read_at = {
496	        claim_id: int(numpy.searchsorted(points, _day_index(one.resolution.by, as_of, days)))
497	        for claim_id, one in claims.items()
498	    }
499	
500	    shape_rows = {one.id: _shape_row(one, settled[one.source], points) for one in ordinary}
501	    spells = {
502	        claim_id: _spells_on(fixed_on[claim_id], arrows_into[claim_id], settled, as_of)
503	        for claim_id in claims
504	    }
505	
506	    return _Setup(
507	        claims=claims,
508	        order=order,
509	        arrows_into=arrows_into,
510	        spells=spells,
511	        settled=settled,
512	        day_zero=as_of,
513	        days=days,
514	        points=points,
515	        read_at=read_at,
516	        shape_rows=shape_rows,
517	        observation_reach=_observation_reach(claims, ordinary, spells),
518	        states=_states(claims, spells, shape_rows, points),
519	        warnings=_warnings_about(graph, claims, days),
520	    )

523	def _ordinary_arrows(graph: Graph, claims: Mapping[PropositionId, Proposition]) -> tuple[Link, ...]:
524	    """List the arrows the arithmetic actually uses, **in the order the map carries them**.
525	
526	    A feedback arrow — a market changing the world it is measuring — is left out:
527	    it is carried as data in this version and worked through by a later stack, the
528	    same way the map's own loop check leaves it out. An arrow with an end that is
529	    not on the map is left out too; it already has its own complaint.
530	
531	    The order is the map's own, and that order means something: folding a branch
532	    appends each `insert`'s arrows after the ones already there, so an arrow's
533	    place on the map is the order it arrived in. That is both a settled order to
534	    add the pushes on a claim up in — so two runs agree to the last digit — and
535	    the tie-break when two arrows undermine a supposition on the very same day.
536	
537	    Args:
538	        graph: The map to read.
539	        claims: Every claim on it, by identifier.
540	
541	    Returns:
542	        The ordinary arrows, in the order the map carries them.
543	    """
544	    return tuple(
545	        one
546	        for one in graph.links
547	        if not one.reflexive and one.source in claims and one.target in claims
548	    )

551	def _causes_before_effects(
552	    claims: Mapping[PropositionId, Proposition], arrows: Sequence[Link]
553	) -> tuple[PropositionId, ...]:
554	    """Put the claims in an order that always works out a cause before its effects.
555	
556	    Ties — claims that no arrow orders relative to one another — are broken by
557	    identifier, so the order depends on the map and never on the order the claims
558	    happen to be written down in.
559	
560	    Args:
561	        claims: Every claim on the map, by identifier.
562	        arrows: The ordinary arrows.
563	
564	    Returns:
565	        Every claim's identifier, causes first.
566	
567	    Raises:
568	        networkx.NetworkXUnfeasible: If the map runs round in circles once feedback
569	            arrows are set aside. Such a map has no causes-before-effects order at
570	            all, and the validity rules refuse it long before it reaches here.
571	    """
572	    walkable: networkx.DiGraph[PropositionId] = networkx.DiGraph()
573	    walkable.add_nodes_from(sorted(claims))
574	    walkable.add_edges_from((one.source, one.target) for one in arrows)
575	    return tuple(networkx.lexicographical_topological_sort(walkable))

578	def _day_index(when: date | None, day_zero: date, cap: int | None = None) -> int:
579	    """Turn a date into a whole number of days after day zero.
580	
581	    Nothing before day zero: a value fixed from a day already gone holds from the
582	    beginning of the window.
583	
584	    Args:
585	        when: The date, or nothing at all, which means day zero.
586	        day_zero: The day the window starts on.
587	        cap: The last day of the window, when the answer must sit inside it.
588	
589	    Returns:
590	        The day's number, counting from zero.
591	    """
592	    if when is None:
593	        return 0
594	    index = max(0, (when - day_zero).days)
595	    return index if cap is None else min(index, cap)

598	def _window_length(graph: Graph, day_zero: date) -> int:
599	    """Say how many days the window runs for: day zero to the last day anything is judged."""
600	    return max(_day_index(one.resolution.by, day_zero) for one in graph.propositions)

603	def _days_to_work_out(
604	    claims: Mapping[PropositionId, Proposition], day_zero: date, days: int
605	) -> NDArray[numpy.int64]:
606	    """Choose which days of the window to work the numbers out on.
607	
608	    Ordinarily every day. Past 180 days that is more points than anybody scrubs
609	    through, so the series is drawn at 180 evenly spaced days instead — **and every
610	    claim's own resolve-by day is always among them**. That is not a nicety: a
611	    tile's headline number is read on the claim's own resolve-by day, and if that
612	    day were not on the claim's own series the number on the tile would not be a
613	    point of the line drawn beneath it.
614	
615	    Args:
616	        claims: Every claim on the map, by identifier.
617	        day_zero: The day the window starts on.
618	        days: How long the window is.
619	
620	    Returns:
621	        The days to work out, in order.
622	    """
623	    judged = numpy.array(
624	        sorted({_day_index(one.resolution.by, day_zero, days) for one in claims.values()}),
625	        dtype=numpy.int64,
626	    )
627	    if days + 1 <= SERIES_CAP:
628	        return numpy.arange(days + 1, dtype=numpy.int64)
629	    spare = max(2, SERIES_CAP - len(judged))
630	    evenly = numpy.rint(numpy.linspace(0, days, spare)).astype(numpy.int64)
631	    return numpy.union1d(judged, evenly).astype(numpy.int64)
632

634	def _settled_days(
635	    order: Sequence[PropositionId],
636	    arrows_into: Mapping[PropositionId, Sequence[Link]],
637	    fixed_on: Mapping[PropositionId, Sequence[Assignment]],
638	    day_zero: date,
639	) -> dict[PropositionId, int]:
640	    """Say which day each claim's clock starts on — the day it is *settled*.
641	
642	    Three rules, in order. If an edit fixed the claim's value, its clock starts on
643	    the earliest day any of them holds from. Otherwise it starts on the earliest
644	    day a live incoming arrow reaches it: the day that arrow's cause was settled,
645	    plus the arrow's delay, rounded up to a whole day. A claim with neither is
646	    settled on day zero, because the map carries no timing information about it at
647	    all.
648	
649	    **Being settled is not being true.** A claim with nothing fixing it is sampled
650	    from its own prior in every draw; its clock starting says only when the arrows
651	    leaving it begin to measure their delays from. Conflating the two is the
652	    mistake this paragraph exists to prevent.
653	
654	    Args:
655	        order: Every claim, causes first.
656	        arrows_into: The ordinary arrows pointing at each claim.
657	        fixed_on: Every value fixed on each claim, in the order the edits were made.
658	        day_zero: The day the window starts on.
659	
660	    Returns:
661	        The day each claim's clock starts on.
662	    """
663	    settled: dict[PropositionId, int] = {}
664	    for claim_id in order:
665	        fixed = fixed_on[claim_id]
666	        if fixed:
667	            settled[claim_id] = min(_day_index(one.at, day_zero) for one in fixed)
668	            continue
669	        arrivals = [math.ceil(settled[one.source] + one.lag) for one in arrows_into[claim_id]]
670	        settled[claim_id] = min(arrivals) if arrivals else 0
671	    return settled

674	def _shape_row(link: Link, settled: int, points: NDArray[numpy.int64]) -> Numbers:
675	    """Work out how big one arrow's push is on each day, as a fraction of its full size.
676	
677	    A plain function of elapsed days, and zero before the cause was settled. A
678	    **spike** is nothing through the delay, then full size, halving every half-life
679	    afterwards. A **step** is nothing through the delay, then full size, held. A
680	    **ramp** climbs from nothing to full size across the delay, then holds.
681	
682	    A ramp with no delay at all needs no special case: the days at or past the
683	    delay are settled first, which for a delay of nothing is every day from the
684	    cause onwards, and the climb is then left with no days to climb over. Such a
685	    ramp behaves as a step, as a consequence of the shape rather than as a rule.
686	
687	    A spike always says how fast it fades — a spike that does not is a fault in the
688	    map, refused by its own rules before it ever reaches here. The line below is
689	    the net under a map that arrived some other way, and it holds the push rather
690	    than dividing by nothing.
691	
692	    Args:
693	        link: The arrow.
694	        settled: The day the arrow's cause was settled.
695	        points: The days to work out.
696	
697	    Returns:
698	        One number per day, between 0 and 1.
699	    """
700	    elapsed = points.astype(numpy.float64) - settled
701	    landed = elapsed >= link.lag
702	    row = numpy.zeros_like(elapsed)
703	    row[landed] = 1.0
704	    if link.shape == "step":
705	        return row
706	    if link.shape == "ramp":
707	        climbing = (elapsed >= 0.0) & ~landed
708	        row[climbing] = elapsed[climbing] / link.lag
709	        return row
710	    if link.half_life is None or link.half_life <= 0.0:
711	        return row
712	    row[landed] = 2.0 ** (-(elapsed[landed] - link.lag) / link.half_life)
713	    return row
714

716	def _opposing(arrows: Sequence[Link], supposed: bool) -> list[Link]:
717	    """List the arrows pushing against a supposed value, in the order they were given.
718	
719	    An arrow opposes a claim supposed **true** when its push is negative, and one
720	    supposed **false** when its push is positive. An arrow of no strength pushes
721	    neither way and opposes nothing.
722	    """
723	    return [one for one in arrows if (one.strength < 0.0) == supposed and one.strength != 0.0]

726	def _spells_on(
727	    fixed: Sequence[Assignment],
728	    arrows: Sequence[Link],
729	    settled: Mapping[PropositionId, int],
730	    day_zero: date,
731	) -> tuple[_Spell, ...]:
732	    """Work out which stretch of days each edit's word holds over, on one claim.
733	
734	    Each edit's word holds from its own day until the next edit on the same claim
735	    has something to say, because a later assignment overrides an earlier one. A
736	    supposition also stops early, on the day the **cause** of the first arrow
737	    pushing against it was settled — not the day that arrow's push reaches full
738	    size, because tying the end of a supposition to the arrival would tie "do I
739	    still take your word for this" to a delay parameter.
740	
741	    A user may suppose a claim again after it was undermined. The second
742	    supposition holds from its own day until something undermines it again, and the
743	    series then reads supposed, withdrawn, pushed, supposed — which falls straight
744	    out of "a later assignment overrides an earlier one" rather than needing a rule
745	    of its own.
746	
747	    When two arrows undermine a supposition on the very same day, the one that
748	    arrived on the map first wins. That is the arrow's own place on the map, which
749	    is the order the edits added them in: the base map's arrows, then each `insert`'s
750	    arrows in the order it listed them. Some settled answer is needed or the badge
751	    would name a different arrow on different runs and a world would stop replaying.
752	
753	    Args:
754	        fixed: Every value fixed on this claim, in the order the edits were made.
755	        arrows: The ordinary arrows pointing at it, in the order the map carries them.
756	        settled: The day each claim's clock starts on.
757	        day_zero: The day the window starts on.
758	
759	    Returns:
760	        One stretch per edit, in the order the edits were made.
761	    """
762	    where = {one.id: index for index, one in enumerate(arrows)}
763	    days = [_day_index(one.at, day_zero) for one in fixed]
764	    spells: list[_Spell] = []
765	    for index, one in enumerate(fixed):
766	        starts = days[index]
767	        ends = days[index + 1] if index + 1 < len(days) else None
768	        undermined_on, undermined_by = None, None
769	        if one.kind == "do":
770	            against = [
771	                (max(starts, settled[arrow.source]), where[arrow.id], arrow)
772	                for arrow in _opposing(arrows, one.value)
773	            ]
774	            live = [entry for entry in against if ends is None or entry[0] < ends]
775	            if live:
776	                undermined_on, _, undermined_by = min(live, key=lambda entry: entry[:2])
777	        spells.append(
778	            _Spell(
779	                kind=one.kind,
780	                value=one.value,
781	                starts=starts,
782	                ends=ends,
783	                undermined_on=undermined_on,
784	                undermined_by=undermined_by,
785	            )
786	        )
787	    return tuple(spells)

790	def _retractions(setup: _Setup, introduced_by: Mapping[LinkId, int]) -> tuple[Retraction, ...]:
791	    """Write down every supposition something undermined, and which edit is to blame.
792	
793	    **Which edit added the undermining arrow is always known**, and that is a
794	    theorem rather than a convention: supposing a claim cuts every arrow pointing
795	    at it at that moment, so any arrow that later pushes against it was added
796	    afterwards, by an edit with a position in the branch.
797	
798	    Args:
799	        setup: Everything chance has no say in.
800	        introduced_by: Which edit added each arrow, by position in the branch.
801	
802	    Returns:
803	        One retraction per supposition that ended, claim by claim.
804	
805	    Raises:
806	        ValueError: If an arrow that undermined a supposition is not in the list of
807	            which edit added what. That is the one thing this file raises for, and
808	            it is a broken promise between our own two pieces of code rather than
809	            anything a user did: whoever asked for this world folded a branch onto
810	            the map and then did not say which edit added which arrow.
811	    """
812	    found: list[Retraction] = []
813	    for claim_id in sorted(setup.spells):
814	        for spell in setup.spells[claim_id]:
815	            if spell.undermined_on is None or spell.undermined_by is None:
816	                continue
817	            arrow = spell.undermined_by
818	            if arrow.id not in introduced_by:
819	                raise ValueError(
820	                    "A supposition was undermined by an arrow that nothing says was added "
821	                    "by an edit. Every arrow that can undermine a supposition was added "
822	                    "after it, so the branch's edits have to be passed in alongside the "
823	                    "values they fixed."
824	                )
825	            found.append(
826	                Retraction(
827	                    target=claim_id,
828	                    at=setup.day_zero + timedelta(days=spell.undermined_on),
829	                    by_link=arrow.id,
830	                    by_claim=arrow.source,
831	                    by=introduced_by[arrow.id],
832	                )
833	            )
834	    return tuple(found)

837	def _states(
838	    claims: Mapping[PropositionId, Proposition],
839	    spells: Mapping[PropositionId, Sequence[_Spell]],
840	    shape_rows: Mapping[LinkId, Numbers],
841	    points: NDArray[numpy.int64],
842	) -> dict[PropositionId, tuple[SeriesState, ...]]:
843	    """Name what each claim's every day is, so the canvas knows when a number would mislead.
844	
845	    On a claim no supposition ever touched, and on any day before one takes effect,
846	    the day is `sampled`. While a supposition holds it is `supposed`, and the tile
847	    shows the word rather than a likelihood. Once something has undermined it the
848	    day is `withdrawn` until an opposing push is actually live, and `pushed` after
849	    that. The gap between the two — the day the world changed and the day the push
850	    arrives — is the honest shape of the answer, not a bug to hide, which is the
851	    whole reason these words exist.
852	
853	    A claim reported to have happened is `sampled` throughout: an observation is
854	    news rather than a lever, so there is no word standing in for a number.
855	
856	    Args:
857	        claims: Every claim on the map, by identifier.
858	        spells: Which stretch of days each fixed value holds over, per claim.
859	        shape_rows: How big each arrow's push is on each day.
860	        points: The days to work out.
861	
862	    Returns:
863	        One word per day, per claim.
864	    """
865	    named: dict[PropositionId, tuple[SeriesState, ...]] = {}
866	    untouched: SeriesState = "sampled"
867	    for claim_id in claims:
868	        suppositions = [one for one in spells[claim_id] if one.kind == "do"]
869	        if not suppositions:
870	            named[claim_id] = (untouched,) * len(points)
871	            continue
872	        days: list[SeriesState] = [untouched] * len(points)
873	        for spell in suppositions:
874	            pushing = (
875	                shape_rows[spell.undermined_by.id] > 0.0
876	                if spell.undermined_by is not None
877	                else numpy.zeros(len(points), dtype=bool)
878	            )
879	            for index, day in enumerate(int(one) for one in points):
880	                if day < spell.starts or (spell.ends is not None and day >= spell.ends):
881	                    continue
882	                if spell.undermined_on is None or day < spell.undermined_on:
883	                    days[index] = "supposed"
884	                else:
885	                    days[index] = "pushed" if pushing[index] else "withdrawn"
886	        named[claim_id] = tuple(days)
887	    return named
888

890	def _observation_reach(
891	    claims: Mapping[PropositionId, Proposition],
892	    arrows: Sequence[Link],
893	    spells: Mapping[PropositionId, Sequence[_Spell]],
894	) -> frozenset[PropositionId]:
895	    """List the claims an observation is evidence about.
896	
897	    Observing something is done by throwing away the worlds it did not happen in,
898	    and that changes what the survivors say about the claim's **causes** as much as
899	    about what it causes — which is why observing reaches upstream and supposing
900	    does not. It reaches the observed claim, everything it leads to, everything
901	    that leads to it, and everything those causes lead to.
902	
903	    **And nothing else, on purpose.** A claim joined to the observed one by no
904	    chain of arrows in either direction, and sharing no cause with it, is
905	    independent of what was observed: the right answer for such a claim is the
906	    answer it already had. Reading it off the surviving worlds only would let a
907	    coin flip somewhere else move a number nobody touched — the locality rule
908	    failing by sampling noise rather than by intent — so those claims are read off
909	    every world instead.
910	
911	    Args:
912	        claims: Every claim on the map, by identifier.
913	        arrows: The ordinary arrows.
914	        spells: Which stretch of days each fixed value holds over, per claim.
915	
916	    Returns:
917	        The claims an observation is evidence about. Empty when nothing was
918	        observed.
919	    """
920	    observed = [
921	        claim_id
922	        for claim_id, stretches in spells.items()
923	        if any(one.kind == "observe" for one in stretches)
924	    ]
925	    if not observed:
926	        return frozenset()
927	    walkable: networkx.DiGraph[PropositionId] = networkx.DiGraph()
928	    walkable.add_nodes_from(sorted(claims))
929	    walkable.add_edges_from((one.source, one.target) for one in arrows)
930	    reached: set[PropositionId] = set()
931	    for claim_id in sorted(observed):
932	        causes = networkx.ancestors(walkable, claim_id)
933	        reached |= {claim_id} | networkx.descendants(walkable, claim_id) | causes
934	        for cause in causes:
935	            reached |= networkx.descendants(walkable, cause)
936	    return frozenset(reached)
937

939	def _warnings_about(
940	    graph: Graph, claims: Mapping[PropositionId, Proposition], days: int
941	) -> tuple[str, ...]:
942	    """Say, in plain sentences, what the reader should be told about this map.
943	
944	    Args:
945	        graph: The map to read.
946	        claims: Every claim on it, by identifier.
947	        days: How long the window is.
948	
949	    Returns:
950	        One sentence per thing worth saying, in a settled order.
951	    """
952	    said: list[str] = []
953	    named = dict(claims)
954	    for link in sorted(graph.links, key=lambda one: one.id):
955	        ends = f"from {_name_of(named, link.source)} to {_name_of(named, link.target)}"
956	        if abs(link.strength) > LOUD_STRENGTH:
957	            said.append(

961	            )
962	    if days + 1 > SERIES_CAP:
963	        said.append(
964	            f"This map runs for {days} days, so each claim's series is drawn at {SERIES_CAP} "
965	            "evenly spaced points rather than one for every day."
966	        )
967	    return tuple(said)

984	def _claim_key(identifier: PropositionId) -> int:
985	    """Turn a claim's identifier into a number, the same one on every machine.
986	
987	    Python's own hashing is stirred differently in every process, which would make
988	    a world depend on when it was computed. This does not: the same identifier
989	    always gives the same number, today and next week, here and in a container.
990	
991	    Args:
992	        identifier: The claim's identifier.
993	
994	    Returns:
995	        A number standing for that identifier.
996	    """
997	    digest = hashlib.blake2b(identifier.encode("utf-8"), digest_size=8).digest()
998	    return int.from_bytes(digest, "big")

1001	def _standard_normal_quantile(share: Numbers) -> Numbers:
1002	    """Turn "how far along a bell curve" into "how many standard deviations out".
1003	
1004	    A published rational approximation (Peter Acklam's), accurate to about one part
1005	    in a billion, which is millions of times finer than the two significant figures
1006	    anything on screen ever shows. It is written out because the only library that
1007	    ships this function is one this project deliberately does not depend on.
1008	
1009	    Args:
1010	        share: How far along the curve, strictly between 0 and 1.
1011	
1012	    Returns:
1013	        How many standard deviations out that is: 0 in the middle, about 1.28 at
1014	        nine-tenths of the way along.
1015	    """
1016	    a = (
1017	        -3.969683028665376e01,
1018	        2.209460984245205e02,
1019	        -2.759285104469687e02,
1020	        1.383577518672690e02,
1021	        -3.066479806614716e01,
1022	        2.506628277459239e00,
1023	    )
1024	    b = (

1064	def _log_odds(likelihood: Numbers) -> Numbers:

1080	    the two loops carry seven digits rather than sixteen and the type checker is

1086	def _fitted_halves(belief: Belief) -> tuple[float, float]:
1087	    """Fit the two halves of a stated likelihood and its range, on the log-odds scale.
1088	
1089	    A stated `{p, lo, hi}` is read as a bell curve on the log-odds scale with its
1090	    two halves fitted separately: the middle at `p`, a tenth of the curve below
1091	    `lo` and a tenth above `hi`. The halves are fitted apart because real elicited
1092	    ranges are lopsided, and fitting on log-odds rather than on probability honours
1093	    all three stated numbers exactly and can never leave 0 to 1.
1094	
1095	    Args:
1096	        belief: The stated likelihood with its range.
1097	
1098	    Returns:
1099	        How wide the curve is below the middle, and how wide above.
1100	    """
1101	    middle = float(_log_odds(numpy.array(belief.p)))
1102	    bottom = float(_log_odds(numpy.array(belief.lo)))
1103	    top = float(_log_odds(numpy.array(belief.hi)))
1104	    return (
1105	        max(0.0, (middle - bottom) / NINETIETH_PERCENTILE),
1106	        max(0.0, (top - middle) / NINETIETH_PERCENTILE),
1107	    )

1110	def _version_priors(claim: Proposition, seed: int, versions: int) -> Numbers:
1111	    """Draw one likelihood per version for one claim's prior.
1112	
1113	    The draws are spread evenly over the curve rather than left to clump — a Latin
1114	    hypercube, which here is one stratified column per claim. Each claim's column
1115	    comes from the seed and the claim's own identifier and from nothing else, which
1116	    is what makes a base world and a branch world share their versions: adding a
1117	    claim to the map cannot shift the numbers drawn for any other.
1118	
1119	    Args:
1120	        claim: The claim whose prior is being drawn.
1121	        seed: The one number every draw comes from.
1122	        versions: How many versions to draw.
1123	
1124	    Returns:
1125	        One likelihood per version.
1126	    """
1127	    drawer = numpy.random.default_rng([seed, PARAMS_STREAM, _claim_key(claim.id)])
1128	    strata = (drawer.permutation(versions) + drawer.random(versions)) / versions
1129	    steps = _standard_normal_quantile(strata)
1130	    below, above = _fitted_halves(claim.prior)
1131	    middle = float(_log_odds(numpy.array(claim.prior.p)))
1132	    return _likelihood_of(middle + steps * numpy.where(steps < 0.0, below, above))

1135	def _draw(setup: _Setup, *, seed: int, versions: int, worlds: int) -> _Sample:
1136	    """Run the two loops: every version of the map, and every world under each.
1137	
1138	    Each claim is worked out causes-first, for every draw and every day at once.
1139	    A claim whose value an edit fixed is that value while the fixing holds, and is
1140	    sampled from its own likelihood otherwise. What is kept from each world is the
1141	    **likelihood** the claim came out true with, not the coin flip that came out of
1142	    it — free accuracy, because the number was already worked out.
1143	
1144	    When something was observed, the worlds it did not happen in are thrown away
1145	    and each version then counts by the share of its worlds that survived. That
1146	    takes two passes over the map: which worlds survive is only known once every
1147	    observed claim has been reached, and a claim worked out before then would
1148	    otherwise be averaged over worlds that are about to be discarded.
1149	
1150	    Args:
1151	        setup: Everything chance has no say in.
1152	        seed: The one number every draw comes from.
1153	        versions: The outer loop.
1154	        worlds: The inner loop.
1155	
1156	    Returns:
1157	        What each version drew for each prior, what each version answered for each
1158	        claim on each day, how much the worlds inside a version disagreed, how much
1159	        each version counts, and what share of worlds survived.
1160	    """
1161	    priors = {
1162	        claim_id: _version_priors(setup.claims[claim_id], seed, versions)
1163	        for claim_id in setup.order
1164	    }
1165	    coins = {
1166	        claim_id: numpy.random.default_rng([seed, WORLDS_STREAM, _claim_key(claim_id)])
1167	        .random((versions, worlds))
1168	        .astype(DRAWING)
1169	        for claim_id in setup.order
1170	    }
1171	
1172	    alive = numpy.ones((versions, worlds), dtype=bool)
1173	    if setup.observation_reach:
1174	        _, _, alive = _one_pass(setup, priors, coins, versions, worlds, alive, reduce=False)
1175	    likelihood, inner, _ = _one_pass(setup, priors, coins, versions, worlds, alive, reduce=True)
1176	
1177	    kept = alive.sum(axis=1)
1178	    weights = kept.astype(numpy.float64) / worlds
1179	    return _Sample(
1180	        priors=priors,
1181	        likelihood=likelihood,
1182	        inner_spread=inner,
1183	        weights=weights,
1184	        survival=float(kept.sum()) / float(versions * worlds),
1185	    )

1188	def _one_pass(
1189	    setup: _Setup,
1190	    priors: Mapping[PropositionId, Numbers],
1191	    coins: Mapping[PropositionId, Draws],
1192	    versions: int,
1193	    worlds: int,
1194	    alive: Flags,
1195	    *,
1196	    reduce: bool,
1197	) -> tuple[dict[PropositionId, Numbers], dict[PropositionId, Numbers], Flags]:
1198	    """Walk every claim once, causes first, working out its likelihood in every draw.
1199	
1200	    Args:
1201	        setup: Everything chance has no say in.
1202	        priors: What each version drew for each claim's prior.
1203	        coins: One number per claim per world, held the same on every day. It is
1204	            also the same in a base world and a branch world, so the two can be
1205	            compared draw by draw and the dice cancel out of the comparison.
1206	        versions: The outer loop.
1207	        worlds: The inner loop.
1208	        alive: Which worlds are still consistent with what was observed.
1209	        reduce: Whether to average each claim down to one number per version. The
1210	            first of two passes does not, because it is only there to find out
1211	            which worlds survive.
1212	
1213	    Returns:
1214	        Each claim's answer per version and day, how much the worlds inside a
1215	        version disagreed, and which worlds survived.
1216	    """
1217	    points = len(setup.points)
1218	    shape = (versions, worlds, points)
1219	    truth: dict[PropositionId, Flags] = {}
1220	    fired: dict[PropositionId, Flags] = {}
1221	    answered: dict[PropositionId, Numbers] = {}
1222	    spread: dict[PropositionId, Numbers] = {}
1223	    surviving = alive.copy()
1224	
1225	    for claim_id in setup.order:
1226	        baseline = _log_odds(priors[claim_id]).astype(DRAWING)
1227	        total = numpy.broadcast_to(baseline[:, None, None], shape).astype(DRAWING)
1228	        for arrow in setup.arrows_into[claim_id]:
1229	            push = (arrow.strength * setup.shape_rows[arrow.id]).astype(DRAWING)
1230	            if arrow.mode == "sustain":
1231	                total += push * truth[arrow.source]
1232	            else:
1233	                total += push * fired[arrow.source][:, :, None]
1234	        answer = _draw_likelihood_of(total)
1235	        # One number per claim per world, held the same on every day of the
1236	        # window. A world is one coherent draw, and a claim that flickered true,
1237	        # false and true again from one day to the next inside a single world
1238	        # would be nobody's idea of a world; it would also make a sustaining
1239	        # arrow's push flicker with it. So the day a claim becomes true is the
1240	        # day its likelihood rises past this one number, and it stays true while
1241	        # it does. The chapter does not settle this; the alternative — a fresh
1242	        # number every day — is the only other reading and it is the noisy one.
1243	        came_true = coins[claim_id][:, :, None] < answer
1244	
1245	        starts = _point_of(setup.points, setup.settled[claim_id])
1246	        for spell in setup.spells[claim_id]:
1247	            if spell.kind == "observe":
1248	                at = _point_of(setup.points, spell.starts)
1249	                surviving &= came_true[:, :, at] == spell.value
1250	        held, word = _fixed_days(setup, claim_id)
1251	        if held.any():
1252	            answer = numpy.where(held[None, None, :], word[None, None, :], answer)
1253	            came_true = numpy.where(held[None, None, :], word[None, None, :] > 0.5, came_true)
1254	
1255	        truth[claim_id] = came_true
1256	        fired[claim_id] = came_true[:, :, starts]
1257	        if reduce:
1258	            weighted = claim_id in setup.observation_reach
1259	            answered[claim_id], spread[claim_id] = _per_version(answer, surviving, weighted)
1260	
1261	    return answered, spread, surviving

1264	def _point_of(points: NDArray[numpy.int64], day: int) -> int:
1265	    """Find where one day of the window sits among the days actually worked out.
1266	
1267	    Every day is worked out unless the window runs past 180 days, when the series
1268	    is drawn at evenly spaced points instead; a day falling between two of those
1269	    is read at the next one along, and a day past the end of the window at the last
1270	    one. Only a claim whose clock starts outside the window can land there, and
1271	    such a claim is not doing anything inside it.
1272	    """
1273	    return min(int(numpy.searchsorted(points, day)), len(points) - 1)

1276	def _fixed_days(setup: _Setup, claim_id: PropositionId) -> tuple[Flags, Draws]:
1277	    """Say which of the worked-out days a fixed value holds on, and what it was fixed to.
1278	
1279	    Each edit's word holds from its own day until the next edit on the same claim
1280	    has something to say. A supposition also stops on the day something undermined
1281	    it, after which the claim is worked out like any other — its own prior plus
1282	    every live arrow, each arriving on its own delay — until that stretch runs out.
1283	    An observation is never undermined: it is news, not a lever.
1284	
1285	    Args:
1286	        setup: Everything chance has no say in.
1287	        claim_id: The claim.
1288	
1289	    Returns:
1290	        Which days a value holds on, and the value itself on each of them.
1291	    """
1292	    days = setup.points
1293	    held = numpy.zeros(len(days), dtype=bool)
1294	    word = numpy.zeros(len(days), dtype=DRAWING)
1295	    for spell in setup.spells[claim_id]:
1296	        stop = spell.undermined_on if spell.undermined_on is not None else spell.ends
1297	        covered = days >= spell.starts
1298	        if stop is not None:
1299	            covered &= days < stop
1300	        held |= covered
1301	        word[covered] = 1.0 if spell.value else 0.0
1302	    return held, word

1305	def _per_version(answer: Draws, surviving: Flags, weighted: bool) -> tuple[Numbers, Numbers]:
1306	    """Average each version's worlds down to one number per day, and say how much they differed.
1307	
1308	    A claim an observation is evidence about is read off the surviving worlds only.
1309	    A claim it is not evidence about — no chain of arrows either way, no shared
1310	    cause — is read off every world, because for such a claim the observation
1311	    changes nothing and reading a subset would only add noise.
1312	
1313	    Args:
1314	        answer: Every draw's likelihood, by version, world and day.
1315	        surviving: Which worlds are still consistent with what was observed.
1316	        weighted: Whether this claim is one the observation is evidence about.
1317	
1318	    Returns:
1319	        One number per version per day, and how much the worlds inside each version
1320	        disagreed.
1321	    """
1322	    if not weighted:
1323	        return (
1324	            answer.mean(axis=1, dtype=numpy.float64),
1325	            answer.var(axis=1, ddof=1, dtype=numpy.float64),
1326	        )
1327	    kept = surviving[:, :, None]
1328	    counted = surviving.sum(axis=1)[:, None].astype(numpy.float64)
1329	    safe = numpy.where(counted > 0.0, counted, 1.0)
1330	    middle = (answer * kept).sum(axis=1, dtype=numpy.float64) / safe
1331	    spread = ((answer - middle[:, None, :]) ** 2 * kept).sum(
1332	        axis=1, dtype=numpy.float64
1333	    ) / numpy.maximum(safe - 1.0, 1.0)
1334	    return middle, spread

1341	    """Average one number per version, counting each version by how much it survived."""

1345	def _weighted_percentiles(
1346	    values: Numbers, weights: Numbers, shares: tuple[float, ...]
1347	) -> tuple[Numbers, ...]:
1348	    """Find the values a given share of the versions sit below, counting each by its weight.
1349	
1350	    Written out rather than taken from a library because the library that has it is
1351	    the dependency this project does without, and because a weighted percentile is
1352	    a dozen lines. Several shares are asked for at once because putting the
1353	    versions in order is the expensive part and doing it twice is waste.
1354	
1355	    Args:
1356	        values: One number per version, per day.
1357	        weights: How much each version counts.
1358	        shares: How far along, each from 0 to 1.
1359	
1360	    Returns:
1361	        One row of numbers per share asked for, a number per day.
1362	    """
1363	    order = numpy.argsort(values, axis=0)
1364	    sorted_values = numpy.take_along_axis(values, order, axis=0)
1365	    running = numpy.cumsum(weights[order], axis=0)
1366	    running /= running[-1]
1367	    found: list[Numbers] = []
1368	    for share in shares:
1369	        picked = (running >= share).argmax(axis=0)
1370	        found.append(numpy.take_along_axis(sorted_values, picked[None, :], axis=0)[0])
1371	    return tuple(found)

1374	def _band(
1375	    values: Numbers, spread: Numbers, weights: Numbers, worlds: int
1376	) -> tuple[Numbers, Numbers, Numbers]:
1377	    """Work out the likelihood and the range around it, with the coin-flip noise taken out.
1378	
1379	    The spread we measure across versions is the spread we actually want *plus* the
1380	    wobble of having run only a handful of worlds under each. Those two add, so the
1381	    second is subtracted and the band shrunk by what is left — the law of total
1382	    variance. A claim whose apparent spread was all coin flips then reports a band
1383	    of no width rather than an imaginary one.
1384	
1385	    Args:
1386	        values: One number per version, per day.
1387	        spread: How much the worlds inside each version disagreed.
1388	        weights: How much each version counts.
1389	        worlds: How many worlds ran under each version.
1390	
1391	    Returns:
1392	        The likelihood, the bottom of the range, and the top.
1393	    """
1394	    # Nothing survived an observation anywhere: every version counts the same
1395	    # again, which at least reports the map rather than dividing by nothing. The
1396	    # world carries a loud warning about it, so the reader is not left guessing.
1397	    counted = weights if weights.sum() > 0.0 else numpy.ones_like(weights)
1398	    weights = counted
1399	    middle = _weighted_mean(values, weights)
1400	    across = _weighted_mean((values - middle[None, :]) ** 2, weights)
1401	    within = _weighted_mean(spread, weights) / worlds
1402	    shrink = numpy.sqrt(
1403	        numpy.clip(
1404	            1.0 - numpy.divide(within, across, out=numpy.ones_like(across), where=across > 0.0),
1405	            0.0,
1406	            1.0,
1407	        )
1408	    )
1409	    corrected = middle[None, :] + (values - middle[None, :]) * shrink[None, :]
1410	    bottom, top = _weighted_percentiles(corrected, weights, (0.1, 0.9))
1411	    return middle, numpy.minimum(bottom, middle), numpy.maximum(top, middle)

1414	def _range_shares(
1415	    setup: _Setup, sample: _Sample
1416	) -> dict[PropositionId, dict[PropositionId, float]]:
1417	    """Work out how much of each claim's band comes from not being sure of each prior.
1418	
1419	    Sort the versions into groups by the number one prior drew, average each group's
1420	    answer for the claim in question, and see how much of the claim's own spread
1421	    those group averages explain. That share is what a later stack turns into
1422	    "where would more homework pay?" — it is worked out here because the sample it
1423	    comes from is thrown away otherwise.
1424	
1425	    Args:
1426	        setup: Everything chance has no say in.
1427	        sample: What the two loops produced.
1428	
1429	    Returns:
1430	        For each claim, how much of its band each claim's prior explains.
1431	    """
1432	    order = list(setup.order)
1433	    if not order:  # pragma: no cover - a map always has at least one claim
1434	        return {}
1435	    read = numpy.array([sample.likelihood[one][:, setup.read_at[one]] for one in order])
1436	    middle = read.mean(axis=1)
1437	    total = ((read - middle[:, None]) ** 2).mean(axis=1)
1438	    groups = min(RANGE_BINS, read.shape[1])
1439	    edges = numpy.linspace(0, read.shape[1], groups + 1).astype(int)[:-1]
1440	    sizes = numpy.diff(numpy.append(edges, read.shape[1])).astype(numpy.float64)
1441	
1442	    shares: dict[PropositionId, dict[PropositionId, float]] = {one: {} for one in order}
1443	    for source in order:
1444	        by_prior = numpy.argsort(sample.priors[source], kind="stable")
1445	        grouped = numpy.add.reduceat(read[:, by_prior], edges, axis=1) / sizes[None, :]
1446	        explained = ((grouped - middle[:, None]) ** 2 * sizes[None, :]).sum(axis=1) / read.shape[1]
1447	        for index, target in enumerate(order):
1448	            share = 0.0 if total[index] <= 0.0 else float(explained[index] / total[index])
1449	            shares[target][source] = min(1.0, max(0.0, share))
1450	    return shares

1453	def _world_from(
1454	    graph: Graph,
1455	    assignments: tuple[Assignment, ...],
1456	    setup: _Setup,
1457	    sample: _Sample,
1458	    retractions: tuple[Retraction, ...],
1459	    *,
1460	    seed: int,
1461	    versions: int,
1462	    worlds: int,
1463	) -> World:
1464	    """Assemble the finished world: a number per claim, a series per claim, and the sentences.
1465	
1466	    Args:
1467	        graph: The map the branch's edits left behind.
1468	        assignments: Every value those edits fixed, in the order they were made.
1469	        setup: Everything chance had no say in.
1470	        sample: What the two loops produced.
1471	        retractions: Every supposition something undermined.
1472	        seed: The one number every draw came from.
1473	        versions: The outer loop.
1474	        worlds: The inner loop.
1475	
1476	    Returns:
1477	        One world.
1478	    """
1479	    beliefs: dict[PropositionId, Belief] = {}
1480	    series: dict[PropositionId, tuple[float, ...]] = {}
1481	    drawn: dict[PropositionId, tuple[SeriesState, ...]] = {}
1482	    evenly = numpy.ones_like(sample.weights)
1483	    for claim_id in setup.order:
1484	        # A version counts by the share of its worlds that survived an
1485	        # observation — but only for the claims that observation is evidence
1486	        # about. For a claim it is not evidence about, every version counts the
1487	        # same, because the right answer for such a claim is the answer it
1488	        # already had and weighting it would only let a coin flip somewhere else
1489	        # move a number nobody touched.
1490	        counting = sample.weights if claim_id in setup.observation_reach else evenly
1491	        middle, bottom, top = _band(
1492	            sample.likelihood[claim_id], sample.inner_spread[claim_id], counting, worlds
1493	        )
1494	        read = setup.read_at[claim_id]
1495	        beliefs[claim_id] = Belief(
1496	            p=float(numpy.clip(middle[read], 0.0, 1.0)),
1497	            lo=float(numpy.clip(bottom[read], 0.0, 1.0)),
1498	            hi=float(numpy.clip(top[read], 0.0, 1.0)),
1499	            owner="model",
1500	        )
1501	        series[claim_id] = tuple(float(one) for one in middle)
1502	        drawn[claim_id] = setup.states[claim_id]
1503	
1504	    said = list(setup.warnings)
1505	    if setup.observation_reach and sample.survival < LOWEST_SURVIVAL:
1506	        said.append(
1507	            f"Only {sample.survival * 100:.1f} per cent of the simulated worlds match what was "
1508	            "observed, so the range on every number here is unreliable — not just the number "
1509	            "itself."
1510	        )
1511	
1512	    return World(
1513	        base_id=graph.id,
1514	        branch_id=None,
1515	        seed=seed,
1516	        versions=versions,
1517	        worlds=worlds,
1518	        day_zero=setup.day_zero,
1519	        days=setup.days,
1520	        series_days=tuple(int(one) for one in setup.points),
1521	        graph=graph,
1522	        assignments=assignments,
1523	        retractions=retractions,
